```{r setup}
library(aprbonuslab)
```

## Introduction

This package includes an implementation of a ridge regression algorithm `ridgereg`, using QR decomposition and implemented as a reference class (RC).

## The data

For this demonstration, the `BostonHousing` dataset from the `mlbench` package will be used. From its own documentation in R:

> Housing data for 506 census tracts of Boston from the 1970 census. [...] The original data are 506 observations on 14 variables, `medv` being the target variable.

```{r}
data("BostonHousing", package = "mlbench")
head(BostonHousing)
```

## Splitting the data into training and test sets

We use `caret::createDataPartition` to split the data into 80% training and 20% testing sets. We set a seed for reproducibility.

```{r}
set.seed(001)
train_index <- caret::createDataPartition(BostonHousing$medv, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- BostonHousing[train_index, ]
test_data  <- BostonHousing[-train_index, ]

cat("Training set size:", nrow(train_data), "\n")
cat("Test set size:", nrow(test_data), "\n")
```

## Linear regression and forward selection

We fit two baseline models on the training set:

1. A linear regression model.

2. A linear regression model with forward selection of covariates on the training dataset.

```{r}

# 1. Generate fixed 10-fold cross-validation indices
# (Ensures all models are evaluated on the exact same folds for a fair comparison)
set.seed(001) 
folds <- caret::createFolds(train_data$medv, k = 10, returnTrain = TRUE)

# 2. Pass the predefined folds into trainControl 
ctrl <- caret::trainControl(method = "cv", index = folds)

# 3. Fit a full linear regression model (using all covariates)
lm_full <- caret::train(medv ~ ., data = train_data, method = "lm", trControl = ctrl)

# 4. Fit a linear regression model with forward selection of covariates
# To satisfy Hint (iii), we define a grid to test nvmax from 1 up to all 13 covariates.
n_covariates <- ncol(train_data) - 1
lf_grid <- data.frame(nvmax = 1:n_covariates)

lm_forward <- caret::train(
  medv ~ ., 
  data = train_data, 
  method = "leapForward", 
  trControl = ctrl,        
  tuneGrid = lf_grid
)

# 5. Verify that forward selection evaluated models from 1 to n covariates.
cat("\n--- Forward Selection: Evaluated R-squared for each subset size ---\n")
# Extract the summary object and print R-squared values to confirm all subset sizes were tested.
sum_forward <- summary(lm_forward$finalModel)
print(sum_forward$rsq)
```

`leapForward` can't fit a model with 0 covariates (`nvmax = 0`), so we compute the cross-validated RMSE of the intercept-only model by hand, on the same folds, and compare it with the best forward selection model.

```{r}
# The intercept-only model predicts the mean of medv in the training folds
rmse_intercept <- sapply(folds, function(idx) {
  sqrt(mean((train_data$medv[-idx] - mean(train_data$medv[idx]))^2))
})

cat("CV RMSE (Intercept only):", mean(rmse_intercept), "\n")
cat("CV RMSE (Best forward selection):", min(lm_forward$results$RMSE), "\n")
```

## Performance on the training set

Let's calculate the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) on the training set for the two baseline models.


```{r}
pred_lm_full <- predict(lm_full, newdata = train_data)
pred_lm_forward <- predict(lm_forward, newdata = train_data)

rmse_train_full <- sqrt(mean((train_data$medv - pred_lm_full)^2))
rmse_train_forward <- sqrt(mean((train_data$medv - pred_lm_forward)^2))

cat("Training RMSE (Full Linear):", rmse_train_full, "\n")
cat("Training RMSE (Forward Selection):", rmse_train_forward, "\n")
```

## Ridge regression with ridgereg()

Now, we integrate our custom ridgereg RC object into the caret framework by defining a custom model list. This allows caret to use our function for training and tuning.

```{r}
ridge_model <- list(
  label = "Ridge Regression (ridgereg)",
  library = NULL,
  type = "Regression",
  loop = NULL,
  parameters = data.frame(parameter = "lambda", class = "numeric", label = "Lambda"),
  
  # Define the grid of lambda values to test during cross-validation
  grid = function(x, y, len = NULL, search = "grid") {
    data.frame(lambda = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100))
  },
  
  # Fit the model using our custom RC object
  fit = function(x, y, wts, param, lev, last, classProbs, ...) {
    # Convert x to a data.frame as required by model.frame
    dat <- as.data.frame(x)
    dat$.outcome <- y
    ridgereg$new(.outcome ~ ., data = dat, lambda = param$lambda)
  },
  
  # Define the prediction function for caret
  predict = function(modelFit, newdata, submodels = NULL) {
    # Convert newdata (usually a matrix from caret) back to a data.frame
    newdata_df <- as.data.frame(newdata)
    modelFit$predict(newdata = newdata_df)
  },
  
  # Set to NULL as this is a regression model (no probability prediction needed)
  prob = NULL,
  
  # Set to NULL as no custom sorting is required
  sort = NULL
)
```
## Choosing lambda with 10-fold cross-validation

We use caret::train with our custom ridge model and 10-fold cross-validation to find the optimal lambda.

```{r}
# Reuses `ctrl`, so ridge is evaluated on the same folds as the linear models
set.seed(001)
ridge_cv <- caret::train(medv ~ ., data = train_data, method = ridge_model, trControl = ctrl)

print(ridge_cv)

best_lambda <- ridge_cv$bestTune$lambda
cat("Best lambda:", best_lambda, "\n")
```

## Performance on the test set and conclusions

Finally, we evaluate all three models on the completely unseen test set.

```{r}
pred_test_lm_full <- predict(lm_full, newdata = test_data)
pred_test_lm_forward <- predict(lm_forward, newdata = test_data)
pred_test_ridge <- predict(ridge_cv, newdata = test_data)

rmse_test_full <- sqrt(mean((test_data$medv - pred_test_lm_full)^2))
rmse_test_forward <- sqrt(mean((test_data$medv - pred_test_lm_forward)^2))
rmse_test_ridge <- sqrt(mean((test_data$medv - pred_test_ridge)^2))

cat("Test RMSE (Full Linear):", rmse_test_full, "\n")
cat("Test RMSE (Forward Selection):", rmse_test_forward, "\n")
cat("Test RMSE (Ridge Regression):", rmse_test_ridge, "\n")
```

## To sum up

- Forward selection kept all `r lm_forward$bestTune$nvmax` covariates, so it gives the same model as the full linear regression.

- All three models do about equally well on the test set. Ridge regression with lambda = `r best_lambda` is only a little bit better.

- All models do much better than the intercept-only model (CV RMSE of `r round(mean(rmse_intercept), 2)` against about `r round(min(lm_forward$results$RMSE), 2)`), so the covariates are useful for predicting `medv`.

- The test RMSE is a bit higher than the training RMSE, which is normal for data the models have not seen before.
